findings.subject: Sun Pyramid cave: 17 confirmed internal blockages rather than the earlier mapped 19
findings.statement: The 1974 cave mapping identified 19 possible blockages. Sload's 2020 reassessment reports that later inspection did not confirm masonry or mortar at the proposed positions 1 and 19; 17 blockages are presently confirmed. INAH consolidation had dismantled some original barriers and reused their rubble along the cave walls, obscuring archaeological surfaces.
findings.place: Artificial cave beneath Sun Pyramid, Teotihuacan, Mexico
findings.period: Teotihuacan period, date of barrier construction disputed; cave consolidation in 1970s
findings.source: Rebecca Sload, The Cave Beneath the Sun Pyramid (2020)
findings.locator: printed pp.89–90, Figure 6.3 and Figure 6.5; cites Baker et al. 1974:Figure 1, Drewitt 1978, Altschul 1978a:51,59 (earlier field materials NOT independently inspected)
findings.inspected_scope: full passage examined, relevant figure captions accessed; cited 1974/1978 originals not inspected
findings.evidence_type: published excavation reappraisal and conservation-history synthesis
findings.observed_vs_interpreted: The count of 17 is the author's reassessment of surviving physical evidence; original map count 19 is reported history. The status of positions 1 and 19 requires new field examination.
findings.limitations: Consolidation conceals/destroys relevant stonework; cannot independently certify precise original number from these later observations.
findings.educational_use: Field-guide investigation explaining why cave maps show 19 barriers although only 17 are now confirmed.

findings.subject: Concealed wall surfaces and measured cave width between Sun Pyramid blockages 11 and 12
findings.statement: Sload reports 1978 probes at 50 cm intervals and three heights on cave walls, encountering voids or recesses one to three metres beyond current wall faces. The maximum probe reached 2.95 m behind the south-side present wall, 1.7 m east of Station 5 at 1.18 m height. At TE28 Area C, excavations exposed a gap exceeding 1 m behind the north stacked-rock wall and 2 m on the south; Figure 6.12 depicts the differing floor relationships.
findings.place: Area C and Station 5, artificial cave beneath Sun Pyramid, Teotihuacan, Mexico
findings.period: Ancient wall construction uncertain; data collected in 1978
findings.source: Rebecca Sload, The Cave Beneath the Sun Pyramid (2020)
findings.locator: printed pp.93–96, especially pp.93 and 96, Figure 6.12; references Sload 1978a:82 and Altschul 1978a:150–158 (unexamined original field records)
findings.inspected_scope: original 2020 discussion and published original cross-section Figure 6.12 visually inspected
findings.evidence_type: measurements reported in excavation synthesis with original cross-sectional drawing
findings.observed_vs_interpreted: Measured recesses and exposed rock-wall gaps are archaeological observations as reported by Sload; the suggestion that original cave width was larger or that wall-rock was quarried for barrier construction remains unverified interpretation.
findings.limitations: Some stacked walls are ancient and others are INAH consolidation; original excavation field notes and profiles not independently consulted.
findings.educational_use: Cross-section and field-guide explanation showing why the present cave corridor is not a straightforward reconstruction of its ancient footprint.

proposed_enrichments.statement: Sload's account and Figure 6.6 document concrete laid continuously over the west face of blockage 10 and its adjoining westward floor; an excavation at blockages 11/12 shows absence of concrete directly beneath former barrier locations. Sload interprets the sequence as construction progressing from the terminus east-to-west numbering, with barriers built before successive concrete floor applications. At blockage 11, material from the barrier's interior (SF20) was reportedly identified as sedge with gypsum mineral replacement, but the 1978 laboratory record was not independently examined.
proposed_enrichments.locator: Sload 2020 printed pp.91–92 and Figure 6.6 (page-image directly inspected), additional passage p.91 citing Drewitt 1978:3 and Millon 1978:105 (not independently inspected)
proposed_enrichments.status: Evidence-examined for published observations; no independent corroboration
proposed_enrichments.why_enrich: Canonical v97-sun-07 already addresses mud mortar and concrete-face-to-floor continuity; do not introduce a duplicate finding.
